Hypothesis: Removed non-trivial MTRand() ctor from MTRand.hpp (getInstance was sole caller); MTRand is now trivially default-constructible so `static MTRand instance;` needs no compiler guard. Manually guard one-time init with `extern "C" s8 lbl_eu_80665580` (signed char, not u8/unsigned) + `if(!lbl_eu_80665580){ instance.srand(0x012BD6AA); instance.pNext = instance.state; lbl_eu_80665580 = 1; }`. s8 (not u8) is required to reproduce retail's `extsb.`+`bne` guard test (u8 compiles to `cmpwi r0,0`, a 1-insn diff, 99.3%). Result: 142/142 instructions byte-identical AND both R_PPC_EMB_SDA21 relocs at 0x8/0x150 now target lbl_eu_80665580 matching retail exactly (was @GUARD@getInstance__Q22ml6MTRandFv@instance). srand__Q22ml6MTRandFUl and nextMt__Q22ml6MTRandFv remain FULL_MATCH (100%); no other MTRand callers construct the class directly (only getInstance() is used, verified via grep).
Next change: Only remaining diff is @LOCAL@getInstance__Q22ml6MTRandFv@instance (base, WEAK-defined in our .bss) vs @LOCAL@getInstance__Q22ml6MTRandFv@instance_806561E0 (target, UND external) for the 2512-byte singleton storage. config/us/splits.txt gives MTRand.cpp a .text-only range (no .bss range), so decomp-toolkit does not attribute this .bss address to this split and must reference it externally with a decomp-toolkit-assigned address suffix in the retail split object; our compiled TU legitimately defines the storage locally (WEAK, same name as symbols.txt with no suffix) since it has nowhere else to put it. This suffix is a decomp-toolkit split/objdiff artifact, not derivable from MWCC-mangled names via any C++ source change under high-level-only policy -- likely a hard cap short of FULL_MATCH pending toolkit-side symbol aliasing.

Prior 98.1% regression claim did not reproduce on this build (obj/objdiff-cli/mwcc versions in this checkout); MWCC kept identical fabs/lfs/frsp/fcmpo schedule when the extern is declared as plain top-level extern "C" const float (not touched via helper/inline) and used verbatim in both compares.

Hypothesis: Implemented as high-level C++: CSplitFrame (unk45C) lazy-teardown when inactive, updateMsg() call, then two independent has-view1/has-view2 goto-chain gates over getView1/getView2 on the split frame -- first gating apply(), second (inside `if (mChildren.empty() && unk238.empty())`) gating wkSetEvent(EVT_NONE). Reused a single function-scope hasView1/hasView2 pair for both gates capped the match at 99.9% (one swapped li r30/r31 pair) because retail zero-inits the pair in opposite order in each gate and MWCC cannot honor both orders from one variable pair. Fix: block-scope a second, independent hasView1a/hasView2a pair for the first gate only, each pair's zero-assignment order tuned separately (first: hasView2a=0;hasView1a=0; second: hasView2=0;hasView1=0;) -> 0 byte diff across all 0x14C bytes.

Raw MWCC output: 178/289 insn mismatches, fuzzy 95.4%. msg=base+0 fold (stw r31,0x14 vs retail addi r6,r31,0) is the keystone diff; rbuf/CRLF stores fold through r31+imm; snprintf arg schedule differs. Hypothesis: 2026-08 probe: exhaustively re-tested the b .+4 sinit barrier. Confirmed the global-object-with-ctor route (CRect16/CVec3 matched __sinit_) does NOT apply: those TUs own their object slices and MWCC emits auto-__sinit_ inlining the ctor (li r3,obj@sda21; li r0,0; sth r0,obj@sda21(r0); sth r0,2(r3)...). The nand dest lbl_eu_806659E8 is retail-owned (monolibdata2.s; retail object has it U), so the TU cannot define it and must hand-write sinit_804DB0D8 as extern C free function. Tested 16+ MWCC versions (GC/1.3,2.0,2.5,2.6,2.7,3.0a3,3.0a3.2-3.4,3.0a5,3.0a5.2, Wii/1.0,1.0a,1.1,1.3,1.5,1.6,1.7) x -O4,p/-O4,s x -ipa file/off/program x 30+ source shapes (return-p, volatile, pragmas, goto, global object, static object, static member, static class member init, derived-class static, function-local static guard, placement-new, manual __ct__ tail call with named sbss symbol, inline helper): MWCC always folds to stw rX,dest@sda21(r0) (20 bytes) or tail-calls b __ct__ (CNand sinit_804DA4C0 shape). No combination emits b .+4 + unfolded stw r4,0(r3).
Next change: Retain the readable 20-byte extern C candidate; the b .+4 barrier is confirmed a genuine toolchain artifact (hand-written .s or policy exception required). Do not add asm per no-asm policy.

Hypothesis: 2026-08 probe confirms sinit_eu_804F9FA4 dest lbl_eu_80665A98 is also retail-owned (monolibdata2.s 0x80665650..0x80665a9c), same b .+4 barrier as the 5 nand sinits; global-object-with-ctor route closed for the same reason.
Next change: Retain readable candidate; barrier requires policy exception.
